newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Anderton seeks to mend fences with Labour.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Anderton seeks to mend fences with Labour.

text.p: Alliance leader Jim Anderton said on Tuesday he was prepared to put aside personal and political differences to counter the "awful" prospect of a right-wing coalition made up of National, ACT and the Christian Coalition.

New Zealand Press Association quoted Anderton as telling reporters during a campaign stop in Carterton that he had written to Labour leader Helen Clark suggesting a meeting within the next few days on coalition prospects.
Anderton said he took heart from Clark's comments on Monday that workers should vote for either Labour or the Alliance if they wanted the Employment Contracts Act repealed.

"We are assuming that Helen Clark, in saying these things, is indicating there is some possibility of a working relationship between the Alliance and Labour after the election," NZPA quoted him as saying.
The Alliance has previously maintained that it would not be part of a coalition government unless agreement were reached before the election.
Anderton insisted the Alliance's position had not changed, but voters were entitled to know when they voted for Labour or the Alliance whether there was a prospect of the two working together.

Clark called off a previous round of talks earlier this year. Anderton said he was prepared to meet Clark personally, or for the leadership of both parties to get together on Tuesday or Wednesday. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
